Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.
 What is The Role 
 Elasticsearch powers search, observability, and AI retrieval (RAG) for the world's largest organizations. We are seeking a Senior Software Developer to join the Elasticsearch Performance team. In this role, you will contribute to performance engineering initiatives through high-quality code and technical analysis. Your goal is to help improve the optimization and predictability of Elasticsearch performance, collaborating with area-specific teams to enhance our software.
 What You Will Be Doing 
 Contributing to core performance engineering initiatives from development to production, focusing on the delivery of impactful optimizations. Executing technical designs and plans for architectural and code-level performance improvements.
 Implementing foundational performance models and methodologies for complex, distributed systems.
 Supporting optimization strategies to ensure Elasticsearch remains performant, predictable, and scalable in diverse environments.
 Profiling and analyzing system behavior to identify bottlenecks in logging, metrics, vector search, and ES|QL.
 Ensuring robust performance benchmarks and regression detection for both stateful and stateless (Serverless) architectures.
 Collaborating with peers across the team to apply performance-focused development practices into new features.
 Contributing to automation efforts by building AI-assisted optimization harnesses that streamline profiling, hypothesis testing, and benchmarking.
 Providing technical guidance and peer reviews to other engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence.
 What You Bring
 You have deep knowledge of Java internals and JVM memory management. You understand how concurrency models work. You can write code that is high-performance, thread-safe, and lock-free. This experience includes working with large open-source and enterprise codebases.
 You have proven experience in profiling and optimizing distributed systems. This includes deep experience with benchmarking tools (e.g., JMH, Rally), identifying performance regressions, and implementing algorithmic or hardware-aware optimizations.
 You have a solid comprehension of distributed systems architecture, including partition tolerance, cluster state propagation, and scaling challenges in large-scale data stores.
 You have a proven track record of using AI or advanced tooling to accelerate optimization, debug complex performance issues, and automate benchmarking workflows.
 You possess the ability to collaborate effectively within a team environment, contributing to the success of performance engineering goals.
 You possess the ability to collaborate across functions and teams and seamlessly transition between different projects, codebases, or teams based on business priorities
 You can work autonomously, drive decisions, and result in a distributed team by leveraging asynchronous, direct, and transparent communication.
 Bonus Points
 Experience integrating high-performance native libraries (e.g., C++, Rust, SIMD-accelerated code) into Java applications.
 Deep knowledge of modern storage engine performance, index modes, or vector search optimizations.
 Experience defining and managing Performance SLAs and success criteria for distributed systems.
 Experience working on the internals of a large-scale data store or search engine.
 Experience working on the internals of a data store or search engine.

 At Export Development Canada (EDC), we empower Canadian businesses to succeed globally. As a financial Crown corporation, we offer innovative financial solutions and expert insights to help businesses explore new markets, mitigate risks, and achieve growth.

 Team Overview: 
 The Model Risk Management team provides independent oversight and effective challenge of models used across EDC. The team maintains the model risk management framework, leads risk-based model validation, and supports sound, transparent decision-making throughout the model lifecycle.  Promote continuous improvement through stronger methods, tools, data, automation and knowledge sharing while preserving the independence of the model risk function.

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. ABOUT THE ROLE

Float’s partnerships channel is one of our newest growth motions, and the one with the most room to run.



Accounting firms, affiliates and technology platforms already use Float as one place to manage their clients’ financial operations while growing their own. The foundation is strong. The playbook is still unwritten.



As Head of Partnerships, you’ll report into our SVP of GTM and own the partnerships channel end to end: how we find and win partners across all three types, how we build a community that makes them want to stay, and how what they tell us shapes the product roadmap. You’ll take partnerships from promising to a meaningful share of Float’s growth.




WHAT YOU’LL DO


WRITE THE PARTNERSHIP PLAYBOOK

 - Create the processes, playbooks and infrastructure to scale from a handful of partners to dozens.

WIN AND GROW PARTNERS

 - Find, win, activate and grow partners across accounting and bookkeeping firms, fractional finance teams and investor networks.

 - Own the full deal cycle, from first conversation to signed partner.

 - Design one-to-many distribution and enablement programs so one partner relationship reaches hundreds of clients.

 - Start with the firms that bring the most reach, then widen from there. Once a partner is live, work with Sales to accelerate revenue through them.


BUILD THE COMMUNITY

 - Run the programs, events and community that make partners better at their jobs and make serving clients easier.

 - Track what each partner type delivers, and double down on what works.

 - Own how Float shows up for partners, in their language, alongside Marketing.


BRING THE OUTSIDE IN

 - Carry market intelligence and partner feedback back into company strategy and roadmap.

 - Work with internal stakeholders to clear whatever slows partners down.


BUILD THE TEAM

 - Grow a small team, shape it around where the channel is today, and decide where you stay hands-on.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 8+ years in partnerships, channel or ecosystem growth in B2B SaaS, fintech or payments, including building a partner program from the early stage

 - A marketer’s instinct for positioning a product for a specific audience, ideally professional-services firms

 - Willingness to travel regularly across Canada for events and partner visits

 - Strong command of AI tools, as both a user and a builder

   - A network in Canadian accounting, bookkeeping, VC or PE circles, or a background as an accountant or bookkeeper
   
   - French proficiency (an asset, not a requirement)




THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF

 The Woodfibre LNG Project is located approximately 7 km west-southwest of Squamish, British Columbia. It involves the construction and operation of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility on the previous Woodfibre pulp mill site, which would have a storage capacity of 250,000 m3 and would produce approximately 2.1 million tons per year of LNG.
 Woodfibre Management Ltd. is a privately held Canadian company based in Vancouver and a subsidiary of Pacific Energy Corporation Limited.
 Position 
 The Shift Supervisor is an integral part of Woodfibre LNG ’s dynamic Operations team. The successful candidate reports directly to the Shift Superintendent . This role will be based on the Project Site, in Squamish, BC., and you will play an essential part in supporting the company’s operations team through the Operations readiness Assurance Phase into Pre-commissioning / Commissioning and Start-Up on into the Operational Phase of the project. During Operational Phase as a Shift Supervisor on shift you will also lead and oversee that the environmental practices and social responsibilities to the community are held to the uppermost standards as set out by Woodfibre LNG. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 The successful applicant will:
 Be part of ORA (Operations Readiness Assurance) Core Team member. Deliver procedures, manuals, e-PTW.
 Support the Operations Management in executing the ORA Plan to ensure readiness for CSU into the Operational Phase of the project and throughout the life cycle of the facility.
 During Project Phase of the facility will attend required HAZOPS/ 3D Model reviews, Operability/Material Handling reviews, P&ID verification and detailed Engineering reviews as requested.
 Key CSU Team member during the CSU Phase of the Project.
 Overall responsibility/ownership for safe production and execution of activities/tasks in the plant operational area during their shift.

 Availability and Reliability of plant and equipment during their shift.
 Support Implementation of the agreed Maintenance Strategy.
 Support PTW including functionality/improvements, isolations standards, competencies, issuing, precautions, compliance, auditing, PTW manuals and authorization.

 Shift Team Competencies and Training requirements are in place and measured. 
 Communicate yearly tasks and targets for all shift personnel under his leadership.
 Develop and implementation of check lists & routines for plant and equipment. 
 Timely delivery of input data and correctness for plant daily shift report to Shift Superintendent.

 Interface with HSSE department for compliance and improvements.
 Interface with other departments for support requirements and documentation.
 Mentor and influence personnel for implementation of best practices.
 HSSE

 Champion HSE as a member of the LNG Operations Team.
 Lead HSE Shift Meeting/ safety walks /audits if and when required.
 Timely intervention to mitigate risks and ensure safety of personnel and plant.

 Safeguarding systems checks lists are implemented/completed by Shift Operations to agreed frequencies and standards.

About Fullscript
 
We’re an industry-leading health technology company on a mission to help people get better. We started in 2011 with one simple idea. Make it easier for practitioners to access the products they trust so they can deliver better care.
 
That simple idea grew into a platform that powers every part of care. Today, more than 125,000 practitioners use Fullscript for clinical insights, lab interpretations, patient analytics, education, and access to high-quality supplements. Over 10 million patients rely on Fullscript to stay connected to their care plans and follow through on treatment.
 
We build tools that make care smarter and more human. Tools that save time, simplify decisions, and help practitioners stay closely connected to the people they care for. When everything they need is in one place, they can focus on what matters most: helping people get better.
 
This is your invitation.
 
Bring your ideas, your grit, and your care for people.
Join us and shape the future of care.


The Role:
Fullscript is how thousands of healthcare providers deliver better care to their patients, and paid digital is one of our biggest growth levers. As Senior Digital Marketing Specialist, you’ll oversee paid strategy across search, social, and programmatic, manage a large budget, and have a dedicated experimentation budget to find the channels and tactics that will drive our next stage of growth. You’ll work with a high-performing agency and a small in-house team, with the autonomy to shape how Fullscript reaches new providers online.
The ideal candidate is a data-driven and strategic marketing leader who can balance hands-on campaign management with long-term strategic vision. You will shape Fullscript’s paid digital approach, mentor a growing team, and continuously evolve how Fullscript connects with healthcare providers online.

What You’ll Do:: Paid Digital Strategy : Includes Paid Search, including Google’s AI-driven formats (PMax, AI Max) and automated bidding, with the judgment to know when to lean into automation and when to take back control. Social, and Programmatic. Strategically drive planning, executing, and optimizing paid campaigns across platforms, focusing on customer acquisition. Ensure cohesive strategy across all channels.
 Campaign Management: While hands-on execution is managed by our agency, this role will be expected to optimize, and troubleshoot digital campaigns across the marketing funnel. Leverage market-leading DSPs, Meta, Google Ads, and Microsoft Ads to achieve Fullscript’s growth goals.
 Test & Learn: Own a dedicated experimentation budget to pilot new channels, tactics, and formats, such as healthcare networks, CTV, LinkedIn, or emerging AI-driven ad products. Design tests with clear hypotheses and success criteria, and make the call on what scales and what gets cut.
 Data Analysis & Insights: Own how we measure paid performance, using incrementality testing, first-party data, and offline conversion tracking to optimize toward qualified providers and revenue, not just leads. Navigate signal loss and healthcare advertising restrictions, and turn large data sets into clear recommendations that drive efficiency and ROI.
 Team Collaboration & Leadership: Work closely with internal teams including marketing, creative, and data, while also managing external partners. Provide mentorship and guidance to junior team members, ensuring the effective execution of campaigns.
 Client & Partner Relationships: Develop and maintain strong relationships with external partners, and cross functional stakeholders. Collaborate on strategy and planning for campaigns as part of Fullscript’s broader marketing mix.
 Process Improvement: Actively contribute to the development and enhancement of Fullscript’s paid digital capabilities, using AI tools and automation to speed up reporting, analysis, and creative iteration. Identify and implement process improvements to automate and streamline workflow to ensure efficient high-quality campaign delivery.
 Budget Management: Oversee your portion of the paid digital budget management, including spend delivery, invoicing, investment, and forecast tracking. Help drive profitability within the department while ensuring campaign efficiency and performance.
What You’ll Bring:: 7+ years experience in paid digital campaign management, with hands-on experience using Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, Meta, DSPs, and other ad-serving platforms.
 Experience in managing $5 million+ in annual paid budgets.
 Strong knowledge of the digital advertising ecosystem, focused on the US and Canadian Healthcare market, with an emphasis on paid search, paid social, programmatic display, and their roles in customer engagement.
 A sharp eye for performance copy, with experience writing and testing ad messaging that drives clicks and conversions.
 Advanced proficiency in Google Sheets and Slides to be able to turn complex performance data into a clear story and recommendations for leadership.
 Exceptional analytical skills with the ability to work with large data sets and derive actionable insights.
 Detail-oriented with a high degree of numeracy and literacy to manage complex campaigns and deliver results.
 Strong communication skills, able to work cross-functionally, and build relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
 Experience managing commercial aspects of digital campaigns, including budgeting, invoicing, and margin management.
 Bonus Points:
 Healthcare B2B and B2C experience.
 Experience and frameworks to apply with A/B testing to refine campaigns and improve results.
 Familiarity with performance tracking tools like Google Analytics and Looker Studio to evaluate paid digital program performance.
 Experience developing and executing marketing strategies for a multi-product platform serving both SMB and Enterprise customers
Compensation Range:: The salary range for this role is between $90 000 and $120 000 [CAD]. Fullscript shares salary ranges to support transparency and help candidates make informed decisions. The range shown reflects base salary only. Additional incentives, perks, and benefits may be available as part of Fullscript’s total rewards package.
 Final base salary depends on experience, skills, and location. We review pay regularly to stay aligned with market data and internal equity. Benefits and total rewards may vary by region.
 Additionally:

⬦ RRSP/401k match – Invest in your future.
⬦ Premium benefits package – Customizable coverage, paramedical services, and HSA.
⬦ Fullscript discounts – Save on high-quality wellness products.
⬦ Continuous learning opportunities – Training budgets and company-wide initiatives.
⬦ Hybrid & remote work flexibility – Your office, your way.

Who we are
 About Stripe
 Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
 Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

 Our Data Science team partners deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. We're looking for data scientists with a passion for analyzing data, building machine learning and statistical models, and running experiments to drive impact. Our Fraud, Losses, and Financial Crime Data Science team builds the models and data products that protect Stripe and its users from fraud, account takeover, and financial crime. We own the full fraud and loss modeling stack - from account takeover detection and card fraud classification to merchant-level loss estimation, unsupervised anomaly detection, and financial crime risk modeling. We partner with Fraud Engineering, Financial Crimes Engineering, and Risk Operations to bring these systems into production and ensure they have measurable impact on Stripe's financial integrity and user trust.
 What you’ll do
 As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling.

 Applying probability distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing to quantify uncertainty and evaluate business outcomes
 Using Python or R for data analysis, data processing, visualizations, statistical modeling, machine learning, predictive analytics, automation, and implementing causal inference and experimental analyses
 Building, training, and evaluating predictive models across regression and classification tasks for bias-variance trade-offs and model selection
 Modeling temporal dependencies, seasonality, and trend decomposition to generate and evaluate time-series predictions
 Identifying structural patterns, clusters, and outliers in unlabeled data
 Deploying models in production and adjusting model thresholds to improve performance
 Designing, running, and analyzing complex experiments and leveraging causal inference designs
 Using SQL and Spark to create, transform, and analyze large datasets
 Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
 Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns.

Fluent in the full funnel, you know paid media, ecommerce, email, loyalty, creative, customer service, and analytics all need to work together — or the customer feels the cracks. If that sounds like you, here’s your next big opportunity:
 AlgaeCal is searching for a top-tier Marketing Leader (Campaigns) to join our team and propel our revenue growth to new heights.
 Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. So if you don’t love digital marketing the way cats love cream, you probably shouldn’t read any further. 
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density. 
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you’ve got…
 2+ years of marketing leadership experience planning and executing D2C campaigns in an eCommerce environment. You’ve led campaigns from the first messy idea through briefing, approvals, launch, optimization, reporting, and “okay, what did we learn?” You know campaigns don’t magically happen because someone made a promo calendar. They happen because someone owns the moving parts.
 A track record of managing six-figure monthly marketing budgets. You've worked with substantial media investments, understand how budget allocation impacts overall business performance, and know that maximizing profit matters more than simply maximizing spend.
 A Yoda-like ability to make strategic, data-driven decisions. When we look at your resume, we’ll see proof that you know how to turn campaign performance data into smart decisions. CPA, ROAS, revenue, customer segments, contribution margin, EBITDA - these numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. They make your brain start whirring.

Paid media, email, ecommerce, loyalty, organic social, affiliates, influencers, customer service, marketplaces - you understand these channels don’t live in separate little kingdoms.  Strategy that converts like a tent revival. You’ve planned campaigns that engage, educate, and motivate people to take action. You understand offer strategy, timing, landing pages, upsells, cross-sells, bundles, coupons, discount logic, and the tiny campaign mechanics that can quietly make or break revenue. You know when evergreen ads, emails, popups, organic posts, or automations need to pause, shift, suppress, or get out of the way so a live campaign can do its job.
 A brain the size of a small planet! In this role, you’ll need to think imaginatively and act strategically. You’ll balance company priorities, finance approvals, product logistics, creative capacity, compliance, customer service needs, and channel constraints without melting into a puddle.
 A results-driven approach to paid media and campaign budget. You’ve worked closely with Paid Media teams, helped allocate spend across campaigns, and know how to look beyond surface-level ROAS. Revenue is nice. Profitability is nicer. You understand unit economics, contribution margin, and why a campaign can look good in one dashboard and less thrilling in another.
 A track record of leadership, mentorship, and cross-functional coordination. You’ve worked with channel owners, project managers, analysts, creatives, and senior leaders to get campaigns out the door without everyone needing therapy afterward. You guide, influence, pitch, negotiate, and push back when needed - without turning into a tiny workplace dictator.
 The ability to put on the Customer Hat at all times. You think through what a new prospect sees, what a returning customer receives, how reward points affect the offer, what happens if someone talks to Customer Service, and whether the whole experience actually makes sense to a real human being.
 Experience designing and executing customer journeys. From first click to final purchase, from campaign email to landing page, from retargeting ad to checkout, from BAU content to live promo, you know how to make every touchpoint feel connected, intentional, and easy to follow.
 A thick portfolio that demonstrates your mastery of all-things eCommerce. Sorry, but if you have to Google what a heatmap is, don’t know why site speed matters, or think an A/B test is just “trying a different headline,” this probably isn’t the job for you.
 A detective’s eye for revenue leakage. Coupon abuse, conflicting emails, poorly timed popups, expired offers, unclear bundles, bad suppression logic, clunky checkout journeys, ads running to the wrong page - you can spot the problems before they quietly drain sales.
 An encyclopedic knowledge of today’s martech, adtech, attribution, and analytics landscape. You don’t blindly trust one dashboard because it has a pretty graph.  A strong grasp of testing strategy. A/B testing, multivariate testing, UX tests, offer tests, funnel tests, creative tests - you know how to plan tests that align with bigger roadmaps instead of throwing spaghetti at a wall and calling it “experimentation.”
 A solid understanding of UI/UX. This isn’t essential, but it’s a definite plus. You don’t need to be a designer, but you should understand how UX and UI choices affect customer behavior, conversion, trust, and campaign performance. And yes, we might swoon if you have it.

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Security isn't a feature at 1Password. It is the product. We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to shape security strategy across the company, working with Security Engineering, who hold one of the highest technical bars in the industry, and with the product teams building everything our customers touch.


You'll be the bridge. You'll understand cryptographic and architectural detail well enough to earn the trust of our security engineers, and you'll translate what matters into clear priorities for feature teams. Just as importantly, you'll bring a deep respect for the customer: a security control nobody can stand to use makes everyone less safe. You'll help us find the design that's both rigorous and usable, and have the credibility to say so in a room full of experts



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Partner with product teams on security early. Work with PMs and feature teams to understand their upcoming roadmaps, identify security requirements and threat-model implications before designs are locked, and make sure those needs are visible, prioritized, and resourced.

 - Align Security Engineering with product strategy. Translate feature-team needs into prioritized security work, and make Security Engineering's priorities legible to the rest of the company so tradeoffs are made in the open.

 - Own an independent security roadmap. Set direction for platform-level security investments, such as key management and recovery, the cryptographic foundations of our zero-knowledge architecture, authentication, and our long-term readiness for post-quantum cryptography.

 - Lead our strategy for the AI era. Define how 1Password approaches agentic access to credentials, secrets for non-human identities and AI agents, and the trust models emerging around tools and protocols like MCP.

 - Balance risk and usability with evidence. Help security engineers weigh real-world risk against user friction, using adoption, support, and telemetry data alongside threat models. Shipping with accepted, documented residual risk is sometimes the right call, and you'll help us make and defend those decisions.

 - Represent 1Password to the security community. Engage with security researchers and our bug bounty program, speak at conferences, and contribute to the wider conversation about where credential security is heading.

 - Raise the bar for product work. Coach PMs on security thinking, challenge assumptions constructively, and set the standard for how security-critical product work gets done.




OUR PHILOSOPHY ON PRODUCT CONSISTS OF FIVE CORE PILLARS:



 - Focus and execution: Can you ship quickly and measure results?

 - Customer empathy: Are you motivated first and foremost to solve customer problems?

 - Effective communication: Can you bring the entire organization, horizontally and vertically, along on the journey?

 - Go to market: Can you understand and drive business outcomes through product decisions?

 - Technology: Articulating how our technology beats our competitors



Product Managers play a highly visible role at 1Password and are critical to the development and execution of our product strategy. As PMs, we are responsible for setting and championing a high bar for our products. At the Principal level, you also set the standard for how product work gets done. You coach, you challenge assumptions, and you make the whole team better. You must excel at prioritization, collaboration, and communication, while holding yourself and others accountable for measuring quality and business results. You will work with Engineering, Design, Security Research, and GTM teams to ensure every decision we make as a product is grounded in our commitment to verifiable security.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 10+ years of product management experience, including significant time on security-critical products or platforms in a SaaS environment. We'll also strongly consider exceptional candidates with equivalent depth, such as security engineers or researchers who moved into product.

 - Deep, demonstrable knowledge of security fundamentals: cryptography, authentication protocols, identity and access management, zero-knowledge and end-to-end encrypted system design, and threat modeling.

 - Fluency in the credential and identity landscape, including passkeys, WebAuthn/FIDO, and the standards shaping how people sign in.

 - A track record of earning credibility with security engineering teams, not just working alongside them.

 - The ability to read and reason through technical specifications, security audits, and cryptographic design documents.

 - Experience making and defending risk-based tradeoffs, and explaining them clearly to engineers, executives, and customers.

 - A history of shipping security features that users actually adopt, and of using friction and adoption data to improve them.

 - Experience setting strategy at the platform or infrastructure level, and influencing roadmaps you don't own without formal authority.

 - Communication that scales from a security research paper to an executive briefing without losing precision in either direction.

 - A strong point of view on how the security landscape is shifting, and the ability to connect it to concrete roadmap decisions.


STRONG PLUS

 - Standing in the security community, through conference talks, publications, research, open-source work, or standards participation.

 - Hands-on experience with AI security: agent identity and authorization, prompt injection, secrets management for automated systems.

 - Experience with compliance and certification regimes such as SOC 2, FedRAMP, or FIPS.

 - Prior work in vulnerability disclosure, incident response, or threat intelligence that gives you a practitioner's intuition.

 - Experience running or working closely with a bug bounty program or researcher community.




WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

 - Working with a passionate, highly motivated Product and Security team that holds an exceptional bar and genuinely cares about getting it right

 - A direct line to decisions that shape the security architecture millions of people depend on every day

 - Empowerment to set long-term security product strategy and drive it through execution

 - A culture where technical depth is respected, tradeoffs are named honestly, and shipping the right thing matters more than shipping fast

 - A collaborative environment where the best argument wins, regardless of title

 Spot clients drifting away and get on the phone before they leave
 Log every call and next step in HubSpot, and own your weekly numbers: contacts, opportunities, referrals, cases

About the Role

   HTS Assist is Hopper's agentic AI assistant for travel, resolving real customer issues like flight changes, cancellations, refunds, and bookings over chat and voice for some of the largest travel brands and enterprises in the world. Voice carries its own product problems, from latency and turn-taking to escalation timing when a human is on the line, and this role owns both surfaces with equal depth.   

  As Principal Product Manager, you will own the customer-facing agent end to end: the conversations, the interface, and the experience our partners put in front of millions of travelers. This is a deliberately design-leaning role, and you will be the day-to-day design decision-maker, shaping flows and interfaces directly in close partnership with partner design teams and our in-house designer.


What would your day-to-day look like

 - Own the roadmap for the customer-facing conversational agent across chat and voice, from intent coverage and conversation design to the interfaces partners embed in their apps and websites

 - Set the product bar for voice specifically, covering latency, turn-taking, barge-in handling, localization, realtime voice and ASR/TTS quality, since a caller's tolerance for a bad interaction is lower than a chat user's

 - Engage enterprise partners through discovery, requirement shaping, and launch decisions, translating partner asks into product choices that keep one product serving many partners

 - Partner with Partner Solutions on implementation and onboarding

 - Drive design daily, working hands-on in Figma to produce flows and wireframes, and partner with design on high-fidelity and production assets

 - Build working prototypes using AI coding tools where they beat a written spec, to test conversation flows and interface ideas

 - Define and defend quality bars with the evaluation team, covering resolution rate, containment, escalation correctness, and conversation quality across both chat and voice

 - Specify agent behavior in detail, including resolution, tone, escalation policy, guardrails, and edge cases, and iterate from production conversation data

 - Stay close to GTM, Partner Solutions, and Success teams, feeding what the field learns back into the roadmap
   
    

An ideal candidate has

 - 8+ years of product management experience, including principal or lead-level ownership of a customer-facing product, with direct experience shipping voice-based conversational products such as IVR, voice bots, or contact center voice automation

 - Hands-on ownership of a production voice product, not only chat or text-based conversational AI, with working knowledge of ASR/TTS tradeoffs, latency budgets, and turn-taking or barge-in design. This is a required skillset 

 - Design fluency, comfortable manipulating design files and producing flows and basic mocks solo in Figma, having operated as a de facto design lead on a lean team

 - The ability to write enough code to get a prototype working without waiting on an engineer, treating AI tools as a normal part of how they build

 - Hands-on front-end experience, having built or shipped web front ends and able to engage engineers credibly

 - Deep partner-facing experience with enterprise clients, ideally in regulated industries, shaping requirements and launch decisions at the product level

 - A data-driven approach grounded in customer service and automation metrics, including resolution, containment, CSAT, and escalation quality

 - Working familiarity with LLM-based products, including prompt and behavior design, AI quality practices, and their failure modes
   

Perks and benefits of working with us

 - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and upsides of pre-IPO equity packages

 - Hopper covers 100% of the premiums for the group insurance plan

 - Hopper offers life, short term and long term disability coverage

 - HSA that covers eligible medical and dental expenses

 - All employees and dependents have access to Dialogue's telemedicine services, anytime, anywhere

 - All employees have access to an RRSP plan with automatic pre-tax withdrawals per pay

 - Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Carrot Cash travel stipend

 - Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk and a work-from-home stipend

 - Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business

 - Open communication with management and company leadership

 - Small, dynamic teams with massive impact

About Hopper
At Hopper, we are on a mission to become the leading travel platform globally, powering Hopper's mobile app, website and our B2B business, HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions). By leveraging massive amounts of data and advanced machine learning algorithms, Hopper combines its world-class travel agency offering with proprietary fintech products to bring transparency, flexibility and savings to travelers globally. We have developed several unique fintech solutions that address everything from pricing volatility to trip disruptions, helping people travel better and save more on their trips.

The Hopper platform serves hundreds of millions of travelers globally and continues to capture market share around the world. The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times and has become largely popular among younger travelers, with 70% of its users being Gen Z and millennials.

While many know us as the Gen Z and Millennial travel app, Hopper has evolved to become much more than that. In recent years, we've grown into a travel fintech provider, commerce platform, and global travel agency that powers some of the world's largest brands.

Through HTS, our B2B division, the company supercharges its partners' direct channels by integrating our fintech products on their sites or powering end-to-end travel portals. Today, our partners include leading travel brands like Capital One, Nubank, Air Canada, and many more.

Here are just a few stats that demonstrate the company's recent growth: billions of dollars worth of travel and travel fintech are sold through Hopper and HTS's channels every year. Our fintech products, including Cancel for Any Reason and Flight Disruption Assistance, have exceptionally strong CSAT because the terms are always clear and customers receive instant, no-questions-asked resolutions. Almost 30% of our app customers purchase at least one fintech product when making a booking, and consumers are 1.6x more likely to repurchase if they add fintech to their booking versus booking travel alone.

Given the success of its fintech products, Hopper launched a B2B initiative, HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), which represents more than 75% of the business. Through HTS, any travel provider, including airlines, hotels, banks, and travel agencies, can integrate and seamlessly distribute Hopper's fintech or travel inventory on their direct channels. As its first HTS partnership, the company partnered with Capital One to co-develop Capital One Travel, a travel portal designed specifically for cardholders. Other HTS partners include Air Canada, Uber, CommBank, Nubank, Flair Airlines and many more.

Hopper has been named the #1 most innovative company in travel by Fast Company. Hopper has been downloaded over 120 million times and continues to see millions of new installs each month. Hopper is now the #3 largest online travel agency in North America, and 70% of our app customers are Gen Z and millennial travelers.

Hopper has raised over $750 million USD of private capital and is backed by some of the largest institutional investors and banks in the world. HTS is primed to continue its growth as the leading travel ecommerce provider in a $1 trillion online shopping category. The Hopper app and website will also continue to be the preferred travel provider for Gen Z and Millennials.

About Faire 
 Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
 We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.
 Role Overview
 Faire’s marketing org runs largely on systems marketing does not currently build. Audiences and attributes, campaign automation, landing pages, attribution, translation, paid feeds, monitoring and alerting: today most of it gets assembled request by request, or waits on a partner engineering pod carrying its own roadmap. The Marketing Engineer builds those systems inside marketing, on Faire’s production stack, and enables marketers to then run solo.
 This is an engineering role sitting inside marketing. You will write production code across Faire’s codebase, own services end to end, take part in on-call, and put agents into marketing workflows with the evals and monitoring that make them trustworthy at scale. You will be measured on whether the marketing org gained a capability it did not have before.
 The surface you own can span various disciplines: Paid media tooling and feed automation, the landing page framework, lifecycle and campaign systems, the marketing data layer, internal platform tooling, and the consumption layer for Faire’s recommendation and propensity models inside marketing surfaces are all in scope. You will help define how we work with our broader EPDD partner teams.
 What you'll build first
 Before you join, these problems will probably have moved, you should be comfortable with that. Below are two current problems we’re looking at solving short term:
 Marketing-led landing pages. Our current marketing led landing pages workflow is slower than it should be for the blog, newsroom and content teams, and for landing page tests in lifecycle and paid we’re often spending more time talking/prioritizing experiments than building experiences for them. You will own this surface end to end, and you will own the recommendation on where it goes next: you might decide between vendor vs. in-house solution, or build a self-serve, agentic landing page service. The outcome is simple, better, faster landing pages, more self serve, and happy partner teams.
 Self-serve audiences and attributes. Our partner teams currently go through us for Audience syncing with paid platforms and marketing led lifecycle. We think this should be a self service capability available to our marketers: whether that's a vendor or in-house, how the data contract gets enforced in code, and what the self-serve layer looks like are all open questions this person will answer to ensure we reach the right person at the right time with the right message.
 Other projects on our radar: a learning loop for generative assets in ad campaigns, improving infra behind core intelligence feeds powering our paid campaigns, real-time recommendation management across lifecycle and paid, and more.
 How we work
 Own services end to end. Design, build, review, deploy, monitor.
 Ship in Faire's production codebase, to Faire's engineering standards, with code review by engineers.
 Sit with lifecycle, paid, brand and product marketing rather than behind a ticket queue. Find the pattern behind the requests, then decide what to build so they stop arriving.
 Put agents into the patterned majority of the queue, with an eval harness, monitoring and a defined failure mode before anything reaches a customer.
 Turn ambiguous asks into a scoped, prioritized plan, and communicate tradeoffs and progress to non-technical stakeholders.
 Qualifications
 Required
 4+ years shipping and owning production software, in or adjacent to a marketing, growth or GTM organization.
 You'll work in Faire's production codebase. Faire’s stack is Kotlin, Java, JUnit, Hibernate, Guice and Jersey, React and Next.js, HTTP, JSON and Protocol Buffers, MySQL and CockroachDB, on AWS.
 SQL and enough comfort in the warehouse to instrument what matters and decide what to build next from the data.
 Depth in at least one marketing platform: a CDP or ESP (Braze, Iterable, Segment, Hightouch), an attribution or analytics platform, a CMS, or an ad platform API.
 Daily use of AI coding agents, plus experience putting LLMs into production systems with evals, monitoring and a defined failure mode.
 A track record of owning a system end to end, including the on-call, and shipping it to non-technical users who then operated it without you.
 Preferred
 Marketplace or two-sided e-commerce experience.
 Production experience with Kotlin or Java on the backend and JavaScript or TypeScript with React or Next.js on the frontend.
 Having replaced a martech vendor with an in-house build, and being able to say what it cost.
 Braze, Hightouch, Google Ads, Meta.

 This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

 Why you’ll love working at Faire 
 Move fast: You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.

 Content people save and share – saves, shares and engagement rate by brand (platform insights)

 Turn the creator and UGC content from our creator programs into organic posts that perform.

About OraLux
 OraLux™ is a US-based oral wellness brand helping thousands of customers support healthier gums at home. We are building a private member community where our customers learn, share their progress, and get straight answers about gum health, and we are looking for a licensed dentist to be its trusted voice.
 The Role
 You will host a live “Ask a Dentist” Q&A session once a week, a maximum of one hour, answering member-submitted questions about gum health in clear, friendly, plain English. Questions are collected and prioritised in advance, so you always know what is coming.
 As a plus, between sessions you will drop into the community forum to answer a handful of written member questions. This is light and async, on your own schedule, roughly twenty to thirty minutes once a week.
 What You Will Talk About
 Gum recession, bleeding, sensitivity, and everyday gum health, explained simply. How members can get the most out of their at-home routine, with honest expectations and realistic timelines. Habits that help and habits that hurt gum health. What members should ask their own dentist at their next visit.
 Important: sessions are general education, never personal medical advice or diagnosis. We provide a full content brief, claims guidelines and disclaimer language. You will never be asked to make product claims or to act as a treating dentist for members.
 What We Are Looking For
 Non-negotiable: you are a licensed dentist (DDS, DMD, BDS or country equivalent) with an active, verifiable license. This search is worldwide and open to any country, but the license is the one requirement we will not flex on.
 Fluent spoken English, comfortable explaining clinical concepts in everyday language to a general US audience. Great on camera, warm, patient, and natural on a live video call. Reliable availability for a fixed weekly one-hour slot, with US-friendly evening or weekend hours preferred, plus stable internet and a decent camera and microphone. Comfortable being recorded, since sessions are recorded for the community and selected clips may be used in our content, all covered in the agreement.
 Nice to Have
 A periodontics background or a special interest in gum health. Experience creating patient-education content on YouTube, social, courses, or webinars. Experience with online communities or telehealth.
 How the Engagement Works
 This is a part-time contractor role of roughly two to three hours per week in total, made up of one live session, light forum participation, and brief preparation. We intend a long-term collaboration on the same weekly slot as the community grows. The position is fully remote and worldwide. Compensation is discussed during the application, so please share your rate expectations, per session or per month.

------------------------------------------
 
Concepteur des Jeux de rôle 
 
Avec de nombreux prix à notre actif, Larian Studios a démontré son engagement envers la création de jeux de rôle de première qualité. Alors que nous nous tournons vers de nouveaux projets, le studio derrière Baldur’s Gate 3 et Divinity: Original Sin 2 recherche actuellement un concepteur de jeux de rôle pour rejoindre notre équipe de conception de monde. Nous cherchons quelqu’un pour nous aider à façonner les jeux de haute qualité auxquels nos admirateurs sont habitués.
 
En tant que Concepteur de Jeux de Rôle, vous travaillerez avec une équipe qui façonne le monde, les histoires et les personnages à l’origine d’aventures mémorables. En étroite collaboration avec les autres départements, le Concepteur de Jeux de Rôle contribue à transformer la narration en jouabilité amusante qui réagit de manière significative aux actions du joueur.
 
Responsabilités
 
• Concevoir le contenu narratif et de jouabilité dans une zone particulière du jeu, en prenant en charge cette zone tout au long de sa mise en œuvre et en garantissant sa qualité finale.
• Assurer un flux narratif cohérent et bien rythmé dans la combinaison de situations, de dialogues et de zones.
• Créer des solutions aux problèmes de design des quêtes et en assurer le suivi de l'implémentation.
• Organiser des revues d’avancement pour votre zone, recueillir des retours des autres départements et travailler avec eux pour atteindre l’état final optimal.
• Rédiger et mettre à jour la documentation, tout en informant les équipes des changements.
• Adopter une approche globale lors de la mise en œuvre de modifications. 
En tenant compte de l’impact sur divers départements, ainsi que de leurs contraintes et priorités.
• Comprendre les motivations et les attentes des joueurs.
 
Exigences
 
• La capacité de diriger un élément créatif du jeu, de communiquer efficacement avec toutes les parties impliquées, de recueillir des retours et de s’y investir jusqu’à sa finalisation.
• L’aptitude à trouver des solutions créatives à de nouveaux problèmes, ou à identifier les problèmes ne nécessitant pas une réinvention totale.
• Une solide compréhension des temps forts narratifs et du rythme.
• L’aptitude à se mettre dans la peau d’un joueur découvrant le jeu pour la première fois chaque jour, en comprenant les attentes des joueurs.
• La capacité à observer les joueurs, à apprendre de leurs actions et à filtrer leurs retours.
• Une grande aisance numérique et la capacité à s’adapter rapidement à de nouveaux logiciels et outils (G Suite, Confluence, Jira, etc.)
• Un souci du détail et une résistance face à la complexité et au changement.
• Une excellente aptitude à la collaboration, ayant des compétences organisationnelles et de communication exceptionnelle.
• À l'aise dans un environnement agile avec des besoins évolutifs.
• Niveau d'anglais écrit/oral de niveau professionnel*
 
Atouts appréciables
 
• Expérience avec les moteurs de jeu, compétences en programmation ou expérience en implémentation.
• Participation à la création de jeux axés sur le récit.
• Expérience approfondie en tant que joueur et créateur de jeux de rôle. 
• Familiarité avec les jeux de Larian et capacité à capturer notre style distinctif.
 
* En raison de la portée mondiale de nos opérations et de la nécessité d'interagir quotidiennement avec une équipe internationale, des connaissances professionnelles en anglais sont indispensables pour ce poste chez Larian.

 Toronto, ON
Hybrid, 4 days per week in office
Full-time
Department: Product
Reports to: Product and Studio Leadership
 About Big Viking Games
 Big Viking Games is a Canadian gaming company focused on building, operating, and growing long-standing online game communities. Our games have entertained players for years, supported by loyal audiences, live operations, evolving content systems, product innovation, and deep player-driven economies.
 Our flagship titles, YoWorld and FishWorld, have served millions of players over their lifetime. These are enduring live-service virtual worlds with rich in-game economies, virtual goods, social interaction, and long-term player engagement at their core.
 We are entering a new phase of modernization and growth, with a focus on stronger player relationships, better service operations, smarter retention programs, practical AI adoption, improved workflows, and scalable systems that help our games and teams perform at a higher level.
 About the Role
 Big Viking Games is hiring a VIP Player Services Lead to own and elevate the experience of our most valuable and highly engaged players.
 This is a hands-on, player-first role that blends VIP relationship management, retention strategy, player services operations, team mentorship, reporting, and cross-functional influence. You will help shape how we engage with top players, how we respond to player needs, and how player feedback informs decisions across the studio.
 The right person is proactive, empathetic, highly organized, commercially aware, and comfortable operating directly with players while also improving systems, workflows, and service quality behind the scenes.
 You will work closely with leadership, Player Services, Product, Live Operations, QA, Engineering, Marketing, and external or distributed support teams to strengthen player trust, improve satisfaction, identify friction earlier, and support stronger retention.
 This is a hybrid role based in Toronto, with an expectation of working in office three days per week.
 What You’ll Do
 VIP Player Relationship Management
 Own and evolve Big Viking Games’ VIP player program across YoWorld, FishWorld, and future live-service initiatives.
 Personally manage relationships with high-value and highly engaged players through thoughtful, professional, and personalized communication.
 Build VIP engagement strategies that support retention, satisfaction, loyalty, and long-term player trust.
 Plan and coordinate VIP outreach, events, promotions, social engagement, special experiences, and tailored communications.
 Monitor player behavior, spending patterns, sentiment, service history, and engagement signals to identify opportunities and risks.
 Support appropriate upsell, re-engagement, and retention opportunities while maintaining a player-first service mindset.
 Ensure VIP players feel heard, respected, supported, and valued without creating unsustainable one-off processes.
 Player Services Leadership and Quality
 Partner with Player Services leadership to improve the quality, consistency, and effectiveness of player support.
 Help refine workflows, escalation paths, service policies, macros, knowledge articles, templates, and communication standards.
 Provide hands-on support when needed, including reviewing tickets, refining responses, identifying trends, and helping resolve complex or sensitive player issues.
 Help ensure players receive clear, timely, accurate, and empathetic support.
 Identify recurring pain points, service gaps, bugs, policy confusion, or product friction that may impact satisfaction and retention.
 Improve how the team handles escalations, difficult player interactions, VIP issues, and high-sensitivity cases.
 Voice of the Player
 Serve as a key advocate for player sentiment across the studio.
 Translate player feedback, VIP insights, support trends, community signals, and behavioral data into clear recommendations.
 Partner with Product, Live Operations, QA, Engineering, Marketing, and leadership to help prioritize player-facing improvements.
 Identify emerging risks before they become larger player experience issues.
 Balance player advocacy with business priorities, operational realities, and long-term product health.
 Help the studio understand what players are experiencing, what they value, where they are frustrated, and what actions may improve satisfaction and retention.
 Reporting, Insights, and Player Pulse
 Own a regular Player Pulse report for studio stakeholders, summarizing player sentiment, VIP insights, CSAT trends, recurring issues, service risks, and recommended actions.
 Use support data, player behavior, qualitative feedback, and VIP interactions to identify trends and opportunities.
 Track the performance of VIP engagement, retention initiatives, promotions, outreach, and player services improvements.
 Present insights clearly to leadership and cross-functional teams.
 Help convert raw player feedback and service data into decision-ready narratives.
 Use AI tools thoughtfully to summarize feedback, identify patterns, draft reports, improve response quality, and accelerate insight generation.
 Team Enablement, Training, and Process Improvement
 Mentor and support distributed or offshore Player Services team members, helping build stronger communication, empathy, judgment, ownership, and problem-solving skills.
 Create and maintain training materials, playbooks, workflows, escalation guides, and service standards.
 Help improve onboarding and ongoing development for Player Services contributors.
 Partner with team leads or external service partners to improve quality, consistency, and accountability.
 Identify workload trends, skill gaps, capacity risks, and opportunities to scale the service function more sustainably.
 Build repeatable processes that improve player support without relying only on individual heroics.
 Tools, Automation, and AI Workflows
 Identify opportunities to improve Player Services tools, reporting, documentation, automation, and workflows.
 Help implement practical AI-assisted workflows for ticket review, sentiment summaries, VIP notes, macro drafting, knowledge management, and recurring reporting.
 Partner with operations and systems teams to improve how player data, service history, and VIP activity are tracked.
 Help maintain clean, useful records of VIP interactions, player issues, retention activity, and follow-ups.
 Ensure tools and workflows support better service quality, faster response times, and stronger player relationships.
 What You Bring

 Experience managing relationships with high-value, highly engaged, or high-touch customers or players.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly, warmly, and professionally with players and internal stakeholders.
 Strong judgment when handling sensitive, emotional, escalated, or high-value player situations.
 Experience using player behavior, service trends, sentiment, or customer data to identify issues and recommend improvements.
 Experience creating or improving support workflows, macros, knowledge resources, escalation processes, training materials, or service standards.
 Ability to work cross-functionally with Product, QA, Engineering, Live Operations, Marketing, Operations, and leadership.
 Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
 Ability to manage hands-on operational work while also contributing to longer-term player experience strategy.
 Comfort working independently, identifying emerging issues, and making sound decisions when priorities are not fully defined.
 A proactive, curious, player-first mindset with strong follow-through.
 Comfort using AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar platforms to improve workflows, reporting, communication, and insight generation.
 Nice to Have
 Experience in mobile, social, casual, free-to-play, casino, puzzle, virtual world, or live-service games.
 Experience at companies such as Zynga, Moon Active, Playtika, Scopely, or similar online gaming companies.
 Experience designing or operating VIP programs, loyalty programs, player events, retention programs, or re-engagement campaigns.
 Experience managing a large VIP portfolio or high-volume player community.
 Experience with customer support platforms, CRM tools, knowledge management systems, social channels, reporting tools, or workflow automation.

 The ideal candidate is a player-first operator who understands that great service is a competitive advantage. They can build trusted relationships with valuable players, handle difficult conversations with professionalism, and turn player feedback into useful insight for the studio.

 High-impact role with direct influence over VIP relationships, player sentiment, retention, and service quality.
 Exposure to product, live operations, player experience strategy, AI-enabled workflows, and cross-functional decision-making.

 Big Viking Games is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible environment for all candidates. We welcome applications from individuals of all abilities and will provide accommodations throughout the hiring process as needed.
